distinct.note: Kleiner Perkins' AdKnowledge is the Palo Alto ad-management company backed in 1997 and sold to CMGI; TCV's Adknowledge is the Kansas City company (now v2 Ventures Group) it entered in 2010.

Kleiner Perkins' Assured is the insurance claims company at assured.com (founded 2019, Bloomberg's $1B round of March 2025); First Round's Assured is the New York healthcare credentialing company at withassured.com whose $6M seed it led in September 2025.
Kleiner Perkins' Bump is the streetwear resale marketplace (sobump.com, YC W18, London); the sibling row is Bump Technologies, the contact-sharing app of YC S09 that Google bought in 2013.

Kleiner Perkins' Coda is the coda.io document company Grammarly bought in December 2024; Insight's Coda is Coda Payments of Singapore ($2.5B, April 2022).
Kleiner Perkins' Drop is Massdrop, the San Francisco community commerce company Corsair bought in 2023; NEA's Drop is the Toronto card-linked rewards app whose Series A it led in February 2018.

Kleiner Perkins' Endgame is Endgame, Inc., the Arlington endpoint security company Elastic bought in 2019; EQT Ventures' Endgame is the Los Angeles product-led sales platform (endgame.io) it entered in 2022.
Kleiner Perkins' Fauna is Fauna Robotics, the New York home-robot company that joined Amazon in March 2026; GV's Fauna is FaunaDB, the San Francisco database company that shut down in 2025.
Kleiner Perkins' Fin is Intercom, renamed Fin in 2026 and bought by Salesforce; Accel's Fin is the AI assistant company Andrew Kortina and Sam Lessin started in 2015, later Fin Analytics.

Seller and buyer, two companies: Kleiner Perkins backed Fleksy Inc. (San Francisco, founded 2011), whose team went to Pinterest in June 2016 and whose keyboard ThingThing took over in 2017 (TechCrunch, https://techcrunch.com/2017/07/25/fleksy-keyboard-to-get-major-reboot-under-thingthing-dev-team/); Seedcamp's row is ThingThing, the Barcelona company that took the product and its name.

Kleiner Perkins' Fortify Software is the code-analysis security company founded in 2003 that Hewlett-Packard bought in 2010; Accel's Fortify is the Boston manufacturing hardware company it lists from 2019.
Kleiner Perkins' Greenhouse is Greenhouse Software, the New York recruiting software company TPG took over in 2021; Seedcamp's Greenhouse is Greenhouse CI of Tallinn (2016 cohort), renamed Nevercode.
Kleiner Perkins' Handshake is the early-career network (joinhandshake.com, $3.5B in January 2022); the sibling row is the handshake.org decentralized naming protocol of 2018.

Kleiner Perkins' Harmonic is the Palo Alto maths AI company of Tudor Achim and Vlad Tenev ($1.45B, November 2025); Lightspeed's row is Harmonic Inc., the listed video delivery company (Nasdaq: HLIT) it carries from 2003.
Kleiner Perkins' Helix is the San Mateo population genomics company formed in 2015 by Illumina; GV's Helix is HELIX RE, the building digital-twin company Density bought in November 2021.
Kleiner Perkins' Instinct is Noah Shinn's personal AI agent company ($10B Series C, 2026-09-28); YC's Instinct is the London crypto trading app on instinct.xyz (team of five).
Kleiner Perkins' Level is Level Money, the San Francisco budgeting app Capital One bought in 2015; Battery's row is Level AI (Ujwal, Inc.), the Mountain View contact-centre intelligence company.

Kleiner Perkins' Level is Level Money, the San Francisco budgeting app Capital One bought in 2015; Lightspeed's Level is the New York dental-benefits company whose Series A it backed in 2020-21 (the First Round row names Lightspeed in that round).

Kleiner Perkins' row is Linear Technology, the Milpitas analog chip maker backed in 1982 that Analog Devices bought in 2017; the sibling row is Linear, the issue-tracking software company ($1.25B, June 2025).

Kleiner Perkins' Motive is the fleet management company formerly called KeepTruckin (Series F at $2.85B, May 2022); Accel's row is Motive, Inc., the service-management software company that listed in 2004 and was bought by Alcatel-Lucent in 2008.

Kleiner Perkins' Optic is Optic, Inc. of San Francisco (Andrey Doronichev, $11M seed in July 2022, now BIOPTIC); YC's Optic is the S18 API change-tracking tool at useoptic.com, New York, since acquired.

Kleiner Perkins' Parallel is Parallel Web Systems (Parag Agrawal, $2B in April 2026); Sequoia's row named Parallel is Parallel Finance, the 2021 DeFi protocol. Sequoia carries Parallel Web Systems under its own slug, parallel-web-systems, which still reads below_1b although its note cites the $2B Series B: a pair this list does not name.
Kleiner Perkins' Parallel is Parallel Web Systems (Parag Agrawal, Palo Alto); YC's Parallel is the W24 healthcare admin company of Paris (beparallel.com).

Kleiner Perkins' Pattern is Pattern Brands, the New York home-goods brand group it backed from November 2018; First Round's Pattern is a San Francisco software company listed in 2017, before Pattern Brands existed.
Kleiner Perkins' row is Pelago, Inc. of Seattle, maker of the Whrrl location app, which Groupon bought in April 2011; a16z's Pelago is a speedrun SR005 cohort company in Los Angeles.

Kleiner Perkins' Phantom is Phantom Cyber, the Palo Alto security orchestration company Splunk bought in 2018; the sibling row is Phantom, the crypto wallet ($3B, January 2025).

Kleiner Perkins' Presto is Presto Services of Mountain View, the printing mailbox for people without computers (listed 2008); USV's Presto is the fleet EV charging company whose seed it led in 2025.
Kleiner Perkins' Presto is Presto Services of Mountain View, the printing mailbox for people without computers (listed 2008); YC's Presto is the S10 restaurant technology company at presto.com.
Kleiner Perkins' row is Resonate Inc. of Sunnyvale, the traffic management software company that listed in 2000 and was taken private in 2003; YC's Resonate is a W26 social content company.

Kleiner Perkins' Rain is the Bahrain crypto exchange (rain.bh) whose $110M Series B it co-led in January 2022; the sibling's Rain is the US stablecoin card company (rain.xyz, $1.95B Series C of January 2026).

Kleiner Perkins' Series is the finance and operations software company of San Francisco (seriesfi.com, $25M in September 2023); a16z's row is Series AI, the AI games engine company it backed in September 2023.

Kleiner Perkins' Signal is Signal Pharmaceuticals, the San Diego cancer drug discovery company backed in 1993 and sold to Celgene in 2000; Battery's Signal AI is the London media-monitoring company (Signal Media) it entered in 2025.

Kleiner Perkins' Signal is Signal Pharmaceuticals, the San Diego cancer drug discovery company backed in 1993 and sold to Celgene in 2000; Lightspeed's Signal Labs is a company launched in April 2026 that it backed at seed.

Kleiner Perkins' Songbird is Songbird Therapy, in-home autism care for children, on the firm's 2022-23 health-care list; Sequoia's Songbird is the open media player it backed in 2006-07, shut in 2013.

Kleiner Perkins' Spot is meetwithspot.com, renamed Upcraft (AI sales agents) and bought by Labelbox in February 2026; Redpoint's Spot AI is the video intelligence company at spot.ai whose Series A it joined in 2021.

Kleiner Perkins' Summation is the AI analyst company (Ian Wong, Bellevue) whose Series A it led in October 2025; Battery's Summation is Summation Legal Technologies, the litigation-support software company sold to Wolters Kluwer in 2004.

Kleiner Perkins' Tally is the San Francisco credit-card debt payoff app that shut down in August 2024 (a16z holds that company as its own row 'tally', also defunct); a16z's Tally Labs is the NFT storytelling studio behind Jenkins the Valet (tallylabs.xyz).

Kleiner Perkins' Teleport is the infrastructure access company (Gravitational Inc., goteleport.com, Oakland; $1.1B Series C of May 2022); a16z's Teleport is the relocation search engine teleport.org (Sten Tamkivi, Tallinn and Palo Alto), bought by MOVE Guides in 2017.

Kleiner Perkins' Teleport is the infrastructure access company (Gravitational Inc., goteleport.com, Oakland; $1.1B Series C of May 2022); Seedcamp's Teleport is the relocation search engine teleport.org (Sten Tamkivi, Tallinn and Palo Alto), bought by MOVE Guides in 2017.

Kleiner Perkins' Trusted is Trusted Labs (usetrusted.com), the San Francisco on-demand child care company Care.com bought on 2018-07-12; Felicis' Trusted is Trusted Health, the nurse staffing platform it lists from 2020.

Kleiner Perkins' Tulip is Tulip Retail (tulip.com, Toronto), store-associate software whose $40M Series B it led in August 2017; NEA's Tulip is Tulip Interfaces (Somerville), the manufacturing software company whose Series A it led in June 2017, valued at $1.3B in January 2026.

Kleiner Perkins' Drop is Massdrop, the San Francisco community commerce company (KPCB a previous backer at the 2014 Series A; bought by Corsair in 2023). Speedinvest's Drop is a 2022 B2B marketing tool for brands; its own note says it is not Massdrop.

Kleiner Perkins backed Syntellia, Inc., the San Francisco maker of the Fleksy keyboard (team hired by Pinterest in 2016, the product sold on in 2017). Speedinvest's row is ThingThing Ltd, the Barcelona company it backed in 2016 that later ran the Fleksy product and entered liquidation in 2025: a different legal company.
